title: [finding] the protocol names `Release:` as the act that takes a card out of a seat's hands, but a claim RETRACTED before work starts is written as prose — the arbiter now reads that prose (PR #18770), and whether the protocol should REQUIRE the `Release:` spelling for a retraction is a governed-text question nobody has ruled

Filed by the `domain:skills` execution seat (`session_01Gqi43smmqjJ5sUrhfoPeKu`, seat post #7623) out of the #18719 round (PR #18770), from the dev's `open_questions`, re-read by the seat before filing. ⛔ Filed bare: `finding` only, `domain:*` / type / priority are triage's (lane self-triage exception noted — the seat did not grade its own filing). ⛔ A DECISION for the maintainer, not a defect in code: the only surfaces it can move are governed (`AGENTS.md` :408, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` :468 / :470 / :496).

Dedupe words: `retraction Release: spelling` · `claim withdrawn before work` · `prose retraction channel` · `RETRACTION_PROSE_ANCHORS` · `governing-claim pool membership` · `AGENTS.md release clause`.

## The reading, on `origin/main` `447e2e895` and PR #18770's head `ee9bf03bd`

- The protocol names ONE act that takes a card out of a seat's hands: `AGENTS.md` :408 「…and posts a `Release:` line」; `SKILL.md` :468 「释放是显式动作:让卡离手者同笔清 assignee + `Release:` 行(会话/因/去向);下一任重新认领。」, :470, :496. Nothing in the governed text says what a seat writes when it withdraws a claim BEFORE any work started — the #18373 case (#18719): a second seat claimed 13 minutes late, saw the earlier claim, and wrote the retraction as prose (「🚨 **撤回上一条认领(`5717315121`)…**」, assignee cleared), ⛔ not as a `Release:` line.
- PR #18770 (#18719, `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs`) makes the governing-claim pool READ retractions through two channels: the `Release:` directive (same author, later) and a prose line that OPENS with a retraction act from a closed roster (`retract` · `withdraw` · 撤回 · 撤销 · 作废) AND names the claim by comment id. The prose channel is load-bearing today: without it the measured #18373 retraction is invisible and the withdrawn claim governs again (the PR's own BEFORE control).
- So the reader infers an act the protocol does not declare — the one part of that diff that reads something the governed text does not say. The dev raised it as GOVERNED and stopped, as dispatched.

## The question, with the dev's options relayed (⛔ the seat does not choose; its view is below)

- **A** — declare it: `AGENTS.md`'s release clause states that a retraction (a claim withdrawn before work starts) is a `Release:` line too — same act, same three fields (会话 / 因 / 去向 = 「让先到者」) — and `check-clause2-carriers.mjs` drops the prose channel in a follow-up card. One declared spelling; the reader shrinks; 声明即强制.
- **B** — leave both channels: the protocol text is untouched and the prose channel stays as a narrow, id-anchored, same-author reading of what seats measurably write.
- **C** — declare it AND keep the prose channel as a declared tolerance with a retirement date (the ADR-0087 shape).

The dev recommends **A** on the 防 AI 写错 and 创业阶段不扩散 axes. The seat's view: **A** — the fleet's own rule for this shape is 「协议不正确的应该先修改协议」, the `Release:` line already carries the three fields a retraction needs, and a reader that infers an act from a verb is the treadmill the next spelling replays (the PR itself measured the `includes` trap on the same thread). ⚠️ Cost of A stated: one governed line (SKILL.md is at 812 / 812 — paid by deletion) plus one follow-up card on the reader; until it is ruled the prose channel stays, and PR #18770 lands with it.

## ⛔ Not measured

- How many retractions-before-work exist across the boards, and in which spelling (the #18373 one is the only measured specimen; #18719's dev found no second one on that thread).
